251	(def beautify-exceptions-middleware
252	  "Middleware for handling coercion exceptions.
253	  Expects a :coercion of type `reitit.coercion/Coercion`
254	  and :parameters or :responses from route data, otherwise does not mount."
255	  {:name ::beautify-exceptions
256	   :compile (fn [{:keys [coercion parameters responses spec-messages]} _]
257	              (when (and coercion (or parameters responses))
258	                (fn [handler]
259	                  (fn
260	                    ([request]
261	                     (try
262	                       (handler request)
263	                       (catch Exception e
264	                         (handle-coercion-exception e identity #(throw %) spec-messages request))))
265	                    ([request respond raise]
266	                     (try
267	                       (handler request respond
268	                                #(handle-coercion-exception % respond raise spec-messages request))
269	                       (catch Exception e
270	                         (handle-coercion-exception e identity raise spec-messages request))))))))})

272	(def strip-params-middleware
273	  "Middleware _strips_ all `:params`from the request.
274	
275	  The purpose is to enforce declarative params on
276	  our endpoints (i.e. you can't use a param unless you declare it
277	  in `:parameters`).
278	
279	  This leverages the fact that the `coerce-request-middleware`
280	  validates declared specs on data in `:query-params`, `:body-params`
281	  and `:form-params`, and moves them into `:parameters`
282	  if the specs all pass.
283	
284	  Without this middleware, it would be possible to forget to
285	  declare a param in `:parameters` and destructure it from the
286	  request anyway, which is bad for consistency and also for
287	  swagger. We want self-documenting endpoints."
288	
289	  {:name ::strip-params
290	   :compile (fn [_route-data _opts]
291	              (fn strip-params-middleware [handler]
292	                (fn [request]
293	                  (let [stripped-params-req (assoc request
294	                                                   :query-params {}
295	                                                   :form-params {}
296	                                                   :body-params {}
297	                                                   :params {})]
298	                    (handler stripped-params-req)))))})

300	(def coercion-options {:coerce-response? rspec/coerce-response?
301	                       :transformers {:body {:default rspec/no-op-transformer}
302	                                      :string {:default rspec/no-op-transformer}
303	                                      :response {:default rspec/no-op-transformer}}})
304

            [reitit.impl :as ri]
            [reitit.ring :as ring]
            [reitit.ring.spec :as rrs]
            [reitit.spec :as rs]
            [superstring.core :as str]))

;; ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
;;                    Router Manipulation / Accessors
;; ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

(defn merge-routers
  [& routers]
  (->> routers
       (map r/routes)
       (map (partial into {}))
       (apply medley/deep-merge)
       seq
       (sort-by first) ;; This is a kludgey way to handle conflicting routes during a merge
      ;; because we can exploit the fact that wildcard `:` will sort "first" and then become
      ;; "last" when we reverse it
       reverse
       ring/router))

(defn- filter-compiled-route-data
  "Same as `filter-route-data`, but applied on compiled route data. Ignores
  `:options` endpoints."
  [f compiled-route-data]
  (medley/filter-kv
   (fn [k v] (and ((disj ring/http-methods :options) k)
                  (some? v)
                  (f (:data v))))
   compiled-route-data))

(defn filter-router
  "Creates a new router by filtering methods where `f` applied on the method
  data returns true. Removes routes when no explicit methods (i.e. methods we write
  using `:get` `:post` etc) match the predicate, and also removes routes when
  no automatically generated methods match the predicate. Methods are automatically
  generated when default handlers are used."
  [f router]
  (ring/router
   (seq (reduce (fn [acc [r d compiled-data]]
                  (let [valid-methods (set (keys (filter-compiled-route-data f compiled-data)))]
                    (if (seq valid-methods)
                      (assoc acc r (medley/remove-keys
                                    (fn [k] (and (ring/http-methods k)
                                                 (not (valid-methods k)))) d))
                      acc)))
                {} (r/compiled-routes router)))
   (r/options router)))

(defn select-routes-by-name [router name-vec]
  (filter-router
   (fn [route] (some #{(:name route)} name-vec))
   router))

(defn remove-routes-by-name [router name-vec]
  (filter-router
   (fn [route] (not (some #{(:name route)} name-vec)))
   router))

(defn copy-route
  "Given a router and a route-path, copies the route data and returns a
  new route definition."
  [route-path router route-name]
  (if-let [existing-route (some-> router
                                  (select-routes-by-name [route-name])
                                  r/routes
                                  first)]
    (let [path-params (:path-params (ri/parse route-path {}))
          specced-path-params (-> (second existing-route) :parameters :path keys set)]
      (if (= path-params specced-path-params)
        [route-path (second existing-route)]
        (throw (ex-info
                "Mount path path parameters differ from specced parameters on original route!"
                {:original specced-path-params
                 :mounted path-params}))))
    (throw (ex-info "Unable to resolve route path by this name"
                    {:route-name route-name}))))

  ;; ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  ;;                             Router Validation
  ;; ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

(defn- missing-specs? [path-params specced-params]
  ;; We enforce path parameter specs of the form:
  ;;   {:parameters {:path {:foo ::foo, :bar ::bar}}}
  ;; Rather than simply `(s/keys :req-un [::foo ::bar])` which is hard
  ;; to introspect without spec-tools
  (or (when (not= (set path-params) (-> specced-params keys set))
        {:unspecced-params (set/difference (set path-params) (-> specced-params keys set))})
      (when-let [bad-specs (->> (vals specced-params)
                                (remove (some-fn s/get-spec fn?))
                                not-empty)]
        {:non-existent-or-invalid-specs bad-specs})))

(defn- all-path-params-specced?
  "Inspect a `reitit` route and ensure that every path param has a
  defined spec or predicate. The expected format for speccing path
  parameters is a map of `:param-name` to `::param-spec`.

  Returns route-data to make things thread."
  [[route-path raw-route-data compiled-route-data]]
  (if-let [path-params (:path-params (ri/parse route-path {}))]
    (doseq [[method {:keys [data] :as endpoint}] compiled-route-data
            :when (and endpoint (not= method :options) (not= route-path "/api-docs/*"))
            :let [specced-params (get-in data [:parameters :path])]]
      (cond
        (keyword? specced-params)
        ;; We want to easily find which keys are specced or not, so we
        ;; require an actual map of `:param-name` to`::param-spec`
        ;; instead of a spec identifier `::path-params` pointing to a
        ;; (s/keys ...) spec. This is because spec objects are hard to
        ;; introspect.
        (throw (ex-info (str "Path " (log/quote route-path) " does not spec all path parameters!\n"
                             "Expected a map, got keyword: " specced-params)
                        {:required-params path-params
                         :path-specs specced-params}))
        (missing-specs? path-params specced-params)
        (throw (ex-info (str "Path " (log/quote route-path) " does not spec all path parameters!\n"
                             "Some path parameters are missing specs")
                        (merge {:required-params path-params
                                :path-specs specced-params}
                               (missing-specs? path-params specced-params))))

        :else [route-path raw-route-data compiled-route-data]))
    [route-path raw-route-data compiled-route-data]))

(defn- ardoq-router-validation [routes]
  (run! all-path-params-specced? routes))

(defn validate
  "Implements `:validate` feature of `reitit`,
  passing routes and options to side-effecting validators
  which throw exceptions if validation fails.

  Executes once routes are compiled."
  [routes opts]
  (ardoq-router-validation routes)
  (rrs/validate routes opts)) ; generic `reitit` validation

;; ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
;;                             Input Validation
;; ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

(def ^:private param-source-mappings
  ;; Mapping between param-source, and the spec grouping
  ;; that governs it
  {:multipart-params :multipart
   :body-params :body
   :query-params :query
   :form-params :form
   :path-params :path})

(defn- specific-response-if-configured [spec-error configured-spec-messages]
  (-> (second (:in spec-error))
      param-source-mappings
      configured-spec-messages))

(defn- extract-message-based-on-failing-param
  [spec-error configured-spec-error-responses]
  (or (specific-response-if-configured spec-error configured-spec-error-responses)
      configured-spec-error-responses))

(defn- ->json-path-part [n-or-kw]
  (cond
    (keyword? n-or-kw) (name n-or-kw)
    (number? n-or-kw) (str \[ n-or-kw \])
    :else (str n-or-kw)))

(defn- ->json-path [spec-problem]
  (when-some [path (-> spec-problem :in seq)]
    (->> path
         (concat [\$])
         (map ->json-path-part)
         (str/join \.))))

(defn- ->problem [in problems]
  (let [loc (second in)
        spec-problem (first (::s/problems problems))
        path (if (= :body-params loc)
               (->json-path spec-problem)
               (->json-path-part (first (:in spec-problem))))]
    (cond-> {:in (some-> loc param-source-mappings name)
             :value (:val spec-problem)}
      path (assoc :path path))))

(defn- find-v2-doc-url [{:keys [request-method :reitit.core/match] :as request}]
  (when (get-in match [:data request-method :swagger :x-public-v2])
    (let [path-part (-> (:template match)
                        (str/replace #":([^/]+)" "{$1}")
                        (str/replace "/" "~1")
                        (encoder/url-encode))]
      (->> ["paths" path-part (name request-method)]
           (concat ["public-api" "#tag"]
                   (get-in match [:data request-method :swagger :tags]))
           (str/join \/)
           (v2-swagger/path->developer-portal-url)))))

(defn- expose-coercion-details? [request]
  (or (config/dev? (get-in request [:system :config]))
      (some-> (get-in request [:ctx :user]) core/ardoq-employee?)
      (boolean (find-v2-doc-url request))))

(defn- handle-coercion-exception [e respond raise spec-messages request]
  (let [data (ex-data e)
        problems (:problems data)
        request-coercion? (= (:type data) ::coercion/request-coercion)
        doc-url (find-v2-doc-url request)]
    (if-let [status (case (:type data)
                      ::coercion/request-coercion 400
                      ::coercion/response-coercion 500
                      nil)]
      (cond
        (and request-coercion? (scim-util/scim-request? request))
        (respond (request-util/json-response
                  status
                  (scim-util/->scim-error status :invalidValue
                                          "Request body or parameters failed validation")))

        (and request-coercion? (fn? spec-messages))
        (respond (spec-messages data))

        :else
        (respond (request-util/json-response
                  status
                  (cond-> {:message (if spec-messages
                                      (extract-message-based-on-failing-param data spec-messages)
                                      "Malformed input")}
                    (::s/problems problems) (assoc :problem (->problem (:in data) problems))
                    doc-url (assoc :documentation {:href doc-url})
                    (and request-coercion?
                         (expose-coercion-details? request)) (assoc :data (str (coercion/encode-error data)))))))
      (raise e))))

(def beautify-exceptions-middleware
  "Middleware for handling coercion exceptions.
  Expects a :coercion of type `reitit.coercion/Coercion`
  and :parameters or :responses from route data, otherwise does not mount."
  {:name ::beautify-exceptions
   :compile (fn [{:keys [coercion parameters responses spec-messages]} _]
              (when (and coercion (or parameters responses))
                (fn [handler]
                  (fn
                    ([request]
                     (try
                       (handler request)
                       (catch Exception e
                         (handle-coercion-exception e identity #(throw %) spec-messages request))))
                    ([request respond raise]
                     (try
                       (handler request respond
                                #(handle-coercion-exception % respond raise spec-messages request))
                       (catch Exception e
                         (handle-coercion-exception e identity raise spec-messages request))))))))})

(def strip-params-middleware
  "Middleware _strips_ all `:params`from the request.

  The purpose is to enforce declarative params on
  our endpoints (i.e. you can't use a param unless you declare it
  in `:parameters`).

  This leverages the fact that the `coerce-request-middleware`
  validates declared specs on data in `:query-params`, `:body-params`
  and `:form-params`, and moves them into `:parameters`
  if the specs all pass.

  Without this middleware, it would be possible to forget to
  declare a param in `:parameters` and destructure it from the
  request anyway, which is bad for consistency and also for
  swagger. We want self-documenting endpoints."

  {:name ::strip-params
   :compile (fn [_route-data _opts]
              (fn strip-params-middleware [handler]
                (fn [request]
                  (let [stripped-params-req (assoc request
                                                   :query-params {}
                                                   :form-params {}
                                                   :body-params {}
                                                   :params {})]
                    (handler stripped-params-req)))))})

(def coercion-options {:coerce-response? rspec/coerce-response?
                       :transformers {:body {:default rspec/no-op-transformer}
                                      :string {:default rspec/no-op-transformer}
                                      :response {:default rspec/no-op-transformer}}})

(s/def ::parameters map?)
(s/def ::required-features (s/coll-of keyword?))
(s/def ::endpoint (s/keys :req-un [::rs/name]
                          :opt-un [::parameters ::rs/handler ::rs/no-doc ::rrs/middleware ::required-features]))

(def default-options-handler
  (let [handler (fn [request]
                  {:status 401, :body "Unauthorized"})]
    (fn
      ([request]
       (handler request))
      ([request respond _]
       (respond (handler request))))))

(def default-options-endpoint
  {:no-doc true
   :handler default-options-handler})

(def default-options
  {:spec ::endpoint
   :validate validate
   :reitit.ring/default-options-endpoint (assoc default-options-endpoint :name :generic-options-endpoint)})

;; ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
;;                           Generic Middleware
;; ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

(def json-encode-response-body
  {:name ::json-encode-swagger
   :compile (fn [_route-data _opts]
              (fn json-encode-swagger [handler]
                (fn [request]
                  (update (handler request) :body json/encode))))})

  (-> (h/request :get "/api/mcp/resolve-entity-by-name")
      (mr/query-string {:entityName entity-name})
      (make-request! h/assert-ok!)))

(defn status []
  (-> (h/request :get "/api/status")
      (make-request! h/assert-ok!)))

(defn root []
  (-> (h/request :get "/")
      (make-request! h/assert-ok!)))

(defmacro with-mailbox
  {:style/indent 1}
  [mbox & body]
  `(ardoq/with-mailbox ~mbox ~@body))

(defmacro deftest
  {:style/indent 1}
  [name & body]
  `(ardoq/deftest ~name ~@body))

(defmacro with-org
  {:style/indent 1}
  [org-label & body]
  `(ardoq/with-org ~org-label ~@body))

(defmacro without-org
  {:style/indent 0}
  [& body]
  `(ardoq/without-org ~@body))

(defmacro with-remote-addr
  {:style/indent 1}
  [host & body]
  `(binding [*remote-addr-override* ~host]
     ~@body))

(defmacro as
  {:style/indent 1}
  [role-or-user & body]
  `(ardoq/as ~role-or-user ~@body))

(defn- slurp-events!*
  [channel first-event]
  (loop [events [first-event]]
    (let [event (util/<!!-or-timeout channel 10)]
      (if (= :timeout event)
        events
        (recur (conj events event))))))

(defn slurp-events!
  [channel]

(ns ardoq.test.ardoq
  (:require
   [ardoq.core :as core]
   [ardoq.persistence.postgres-entity :as entity]

   [ardoq.service.housekeeping-service :as housekeeping-service]
   [ardoq.test.helper :as h]
   [ardoq.utils.random-utils :as random]
   [clojure.test :as test]))

(def ^:dynamic *handler* nil)
(def ^:dynamic *ctx* nil)
(def ^:dynamic *user* nil)
(def ^:dynamic *org-override* nil)

(defmacro with-preserved-super-admin-privileges
  {:style/indent 0}
  [& body]
  `(do
     (require 'ardoq.middleware)
     (with-redefs [~'ardoq.login.middleware/revoke-super-power?
                   ;; This functionality is only active for the prod env,
                   ;; but we don't want our integration tests to be
                   ;; affected by this, but instead assume that we've
                   ;; logged in using SSO.
                   (constantly false)]
       ~@body)))

(defmacro with-system
  "Please don't use this outside of this ns"
  {:style/indent 1}
  [cfg & body]
  (if-let [borrowed-sys (get cfg :borrowed-system)]
    `(h/with-borrowed-system ~borrowed-sys
       (binding [*system* ~borrowed-sys
                 *handler* (h/secured-handler ~borrowed-sys)
                 *ctx* (housekeeping-service/ctx! (:housekeeping-service ~borrowed-sys))]
         (with-preserved-super-admin-privileges
           ~@body)))
    `(let [config# (get ~cfg :config {})]
       (try
         (h/with-system [system# (h/test-system config#)]
           (binding [*system* system#
                     *handler* (h/secured-handler system#)
                     *ctx* (housekeeping-service/ctx! (:housekeeping-service system#))]
             (with-preserved-super-admin-privileges

         (catch Exception e#

  release it via `(h/release-captured-test-system!)`. Notice that a captured system will prevent
  any tests from running until released.

  You can also run a test with a pre-created system, without it being started or stopped here:

# Nuggets — investigator, 2026-09-16

Context: harvesting undocumented conventions/traps in ardoq-api, checked against CLAUDE.md, test/CLAUDE.md, ai-features.md, backend-coding-conventions.md, README.md, and skill frontmatters first.

## Route handlers must use `ardoq.test.ardoq/deftest` (or `ardoq.test.api/deftest`), never plain `clojure.test/deftest`

- **Kind:** trap
- **Applies to:** all of `test/`
- **Source:** test/ardoq/test/ardoq.clj:54-75 (defmacro deftest wraps body in `with-system`, binding `*ctx*`/`*handler*`/`*user*`); `.clj-kondo/config.edn:19-20` lints both as `clojure.test/deftest`
- **Confidence:** verified — macro definition read in full; both variants configured in kondo `:lint-as`
- **Nugget:** A plain `clojure.test/deftest` compiles but never gets a running system/ctx bound — tests relying on `*ctx*`, DB, or the handler will fail or silently no-op. Always require the domain-specific `deftest` (`ardoq.test.ardoq` or `ardoq.test.api`). Test metadata like `^{:system-config h/real-job-service-config}` and `:unstrument` only work through this macro.
- **Comment:** Not mentioned in test/CLAUDE.md, which covers helpers/assertions/mocking but not the deftest macro itself.

## `:performance`-tagged tests are skipped in CI (kaocha) but still run under plain `lein test`

- **Kind:** test
- **Applies to:** repo-wide test running
- **Source:** tests.edn:6-7 (`:kaocha.filter/skip-meta [:performance]`); project.clj:244-246,258 (`:kaocha` profile/alias, `kaocha-retry` plugin)
- **Confidence:** verified in config, single cross-reference (tests.edn comment points at `ardoq.integrations.spreadsheet.test-references-import-allocations`)
- **Nugget:** CI runs `lein kaocha`, which skips any test with `^:performance` metadata (allocation/timing tests — run those manually from the REPL). `lein test` (the plain clojure.test runner used in local dev per README) has no such filter and will execute them, so a locally-failing performance test may not be why CI is red, and vice versa.
- **Comment:** kaocha-retry plugin is also configured, meaning CI silently retries failing tests — a flaky test may pass CI without investigation.

## Every reitit route with path params must fully spec them as an explicit map, or startup fails

- **Kind:** structure
- **Applies to:** all route registration under `src/ardoq/**/*_api.clj`, validated centrally
